references.text: The rich man's inner reflection in Luke 12:17 leads directly to his decision to tear down and build larger. He reasons with himself about what he should do with his abundance.
Proverbs 27:1 warns against boasting about tomorrow, for one does not know what a day may bring – a warning that fits directly with the rich man's confident plans.
Isaiah 5:8 pronounces a woe upon those who add house to house and field to field until there is no more room, which reflects the rich man's desire to gather more and more.
Deuteronomy 28:8 speaks of the Lord's blessing over storehouses. The rich man plans to tear down his barns and build larger ones, but he ignores that it is God who gives blessing over what is stored.
James 4:13-16 warns against planning the future with self-confidence and without taking God's will into account – an attitude similar to the rich man's confident plans to tear down and build larger.
The preacher in Ecclesiastes 2:4-6 describes his great building projects and accumulations, but concludes that all is vanity. The rich man's plans to build larger barns reflect this futile striving.
Habakkuk 2:5-9 condemns the one who gathers for himself what does not belong to him and who collects unjust gain for his house. This sheds light on the rich man's greed.

In Luke 12:21, Jesus gives the concluding comment to the parable: So it is with the one who stores up treasures for themselves and is not rich toward God. The rich man's building of larger barns is an example of this.
Proverbs 11:28 says that the one who trusts in their wealth will fall, while the righteous will flourish like leaves. The rich man's plans express exactly such trust in material abundance.
In Genesis 41:35-36, Joseph gathers grain into storehouses as provision for the land. In contrast to the rich man who gathers for himself, Joseph gathers to save others through the famine.
